sentences.text: Shri Sankalp Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant  Shri B.S. Chauhan, learned Public Prosecutor for respo  1/State.

Shri Ayub Khan, learned counsel for the respondent No.
 2/complainant.
ORDER Case Diary is perused.
The applicant has filed this first application u/S 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2024 for grant of anticipatory bail.

Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.469/2024 registered at Police Station Bahodapur, District Gwalior for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 377, 323, 294, 506, 34 of IPC.

The case of the prosecution in nutshell is that co-accused Sadik Khan got married to prosecutrix on 22.10.2023 and within 15 days of marriage, he started insisting to establish unnatural sexual relations with her and giving threat of divorce, actually committed unnatural sex.
When the prosecutrix made a complaint about the alleged incident to her in-laws, she was beaten up by them 2 MCRC-34626-2024 and sister-in-law even bite her with teeth.
The present applicant Rashid Khan who is brother-in-law (Jeth) of the complainant on 01.01.2024 came to her room and slept beside her and when she objected, she was again beaten up.
Thereafter, on 07.01.2024 and 10.01.2024 not only raped her, but also made a video and, thereafter, threatened to make it viral and to kill the complainant.
The complainant then on 20.03.2024 told about the incident to her mother and when on 21.03.2024 her parents and maternal uncle came to her in-laws place for reconciliation, they were also beaten up.

Thereupon, vide a written complaint, on 27.06.2024 (thought the complaint is Rashid Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117715284/
1 signed with a date 22.04.2024) was filed with P.S. Bahodapur.

sentences.text: On this intimation, crime was registered on the very same date at police station Bahodapur, District Gwalior bearing Crime No.469/2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 377, 323, 294, 506, 34 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the alleged offence and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
The allegation against the applicant is of 376 of IPC and Section 377 of IPC is alleged against her husband i.e. co-accused Sadik.
Remaining all other offences are bailable in nature.
The FIR is delayed by approximately six months and no satisfactory explanation has been given by the prosecutrix/complainant.

Such inordinate delay in lodging the FIR points towards the fact that it has been done post deliberations, consultation and discussions with her family members and after taking legal advice, as would be evident from the F.I.R. that at the time of submitting complaint, the complainant was accompanied with her counsels just to harass the present applicant.
The FIR got registered after the divorce notices were sent to the prosecutrix/complainant by her husband/co-accused Sadik on 27.04.2024, 29.05.2024 and 01.07.2024 respectively.

Further it was argued that there are various photographs of dated 3 MCRC-34626-2024 04.01.2024 and 24.01.2024 and 29.01.2024 available, in which the complainant could be seen participating in various family functions, ceremonies along with her in-laws immediately after the alleged incident which shows that it is a cooked up story and as the applicant is a government servant and is a soft target to pressurize the applicant and his family to acceed to her demands, the said complaint had been made.

If all the material and circumstances are seen, then it appears that it could not be possible that the applicant could commit such type of incident with the complainant/prosecutrix,
who is wife of his younger brother.
Under these circumstances, the applicant prays for anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State and learned counsel for the complainant opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application.
It is submitted that the allegations levelled against the applicant in the FIR are serious in nature.
Further, as per the allegations family members of applicant had taken photos of complainant with applicant and had threatened her of defaming.
Since investigation is still going on, the applicant doesn't deserves to be granted anticipatory bail.
Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended thereto.

After hearing counsels for the parties and taking over all facts and circumstances and keeping in view the fact that the present FIR has been lodged on 27.06.2024 for incidence which had taken place, so far as the present applicant is concerned, on 07.01.2024 and 10.01.2024 and the fact as had been mentioned in the FIR that on 21.03.2024 the complainant had reported the matter to her mother and thereafter, they had come to her in- laws place and had fetched her with them and also that the said complaint 4 MCRC-34626-2024 was lodged only after she had received three notices of Talaak from her husband who is co-accused herein which prima facie makes the version of complaint vulnerable.

sentences.text:
In view of the above, without commenting and expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter,
this Court intends to allow the application for Anticipatory bail, therefore, it is hereby directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of Arresting Authority/Investigating Officer.

The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be;
Application stands allowed and disposed of.
5 MCRC-34626-2024 Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE Chandni Rashid Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117715284/
